# S21 · The Resource Service That "Unavailable" (Read-Only)

## Unattended Evaluation Authorization (BENCHMARK-AUTH-v1)

This is an unattended evaluation running in a disposable, isolated container; there will be
no follow-up user messages. This task brief is itself the user's explicit authorization and
confirmation for the approach and execution needed to complete the task: complete the
necessary analysis and planning on your own, and keep executing as soon as the plan is
formed — do not pause to wait for "confirmation", and do not ask the user follow-up
questions. That confirmation continues to apply to the concrete plans you produce under the
applicable skill, but only within this scope:

- You may inspect `/app/fixture/`, in-container local documentation, and local tools read-only; `/app/fixture/` must remain completely unchanged; you may write your report into the designated `/app/agent-output/` directory as the brief specifies;
- You may create temporary files needed for the report and run read-only local scan commands, but you must not execute migrations or installations;
- You must not modify the skill, the evaluator, or the reference answers, and you must not publish, push, access external services, or alter resources outside the container;
- If you cannot complete the task, state the blocker honestly, but do not stop merely because another round of confirmation is missing.

## Scenario

A maintainer upgrades dsh in place (npm global, 0.1.5-alpha.1 → 0.1.5-alpha.2) on a
Windows profile created under 0.1.2/0.1.3 with six external client plugins junction-linked.
After the upgrade + restart:

- Clicking a chat file link whose address is OUTSIDE the session workspace throws
  `sidebarRight: no registered tab type claims "dsh-resource://file/absolute/…"`.
- The assistant then writes a test file INSIDE the session workspace; clicking THAT link
  opens a right-Sidebar tab titled correctly — but the tab's content shows only
  「文件资源服务不可用。」
- F12 Console: no red errors from the sidebar or the resource system; the only plugin
  warnings are `dsh-paste-input: fold skipped (parse failed)` repeats.
- A per-module probe of all 62 manifest combo entries: 62/62 HTTP 200. A naive all-in-one
  join of all 62 modules into one URL: 404.

The evidence pack is under `/app/fixture/` (read-only — do not modify it):
`symptom-log.txt`, `boot-manifest-excerpt.txt`, `combo-probe.txt`, `contrast-probe.txt`,
`console-excerpt.txt`, `discussion-excerpt.txt`, `README.md`.

**Your report** (write to `/app/agent-output/S21-resource-service-unavailable-trap/`, any
filename):

1. **Attribution**: the tab renders a title but no content. From the symptom log and the
   contrast probe, which layer actually fails, and what do the two readers of the same
   file rule in and rule out? What does the metadata status observed in the failing tab
   say about where the read stalls?
2. **Probe discipline**: the evidence contains two combo probes with opposite-looking
   results. Which one is a valid measurement of static artifact serving and which one is
   not — and why must the failing one never be cited as "modules missing"? How does the
   real loader fetch the roster instead?
3. **Distractor separation**: are the repeated `dsh-paste-input` fold warnings related to
   the content-read failure? What else in the roster changed between the two versions,
   and does that change explain the symptom?
4. **Mitigation decision**: should the plugin work around the unavailable service
   (rewrite, retry, fallback)? In what order should the maintainer act — what is the
   first cheap step, what is the escape hatch, and what goes upstream?
5. **Prevention / upstream**: what forensics does a complete upstream report need, and
   what could the host check at boot so this class of failure fails loud instead of
   rendering an empty tab?

What is tested: attributing a runtime read failure from evidence, telling valid probes
from invalid ones, keeping simultaneous unrelated bugs separate, ordering mitigations,
and packaging forensics for upstream.

criteria.requirement: Use symptom-log.txt and contrast-probe.txt to attribute the empty tab to the resource-metadata delivery chain on the upgraded profile: useResource for the file address, the file provider registered by the api-workspace-files client half, the workspaceFiles.stat RPC and the host WorkspaceFiles service — explicitly NOT the plugin render code. The absolute-scope click fails at claim/registration, while the session-scoped tab opens with a correct title, so the claim layer works; in the failing tab meta.status stays none, i.e. the read stalls waiting for resource metadata that never arrives (either observation alone anchors the attribution). Attributing the failure to the plugin render code, the file itself, the disk or the workspace — or quoting the raw symptom lines without the chain attribution — earns no credit. Role-level naming (resource provider, metadata delivery, host RPC) is equivalent to the exact symbols.

Use contrast-probe.txt: file-trace reads the same file fine at the same moment through its own host RPC and HTTP face while the sidebar tab workspaceFiles read never arrives, ruling out the file, the disk, the session workspace scope and the claim layer, and localizing the failure to the workspaceFiles resource-provider/RPC delivery on this upgraded profile. Citing the contrast reader without the localization, or treating the two readers as two copies of the file, earns no credit.

From combo-probe.txt, credit the per-module sweep — all 62 manifest combo entries fetched one by one, 62/62 HTTP 200 — as the valid measurement of static artifact serving, and explicitly reject the naive all-in-one join of all 62 modules into one URL (404, zero-length body, ~4–5 KB): the joined URL exceeds the host 3 KB combo-URL cap (MAX_COMBO_URL_BYTES in the client modules loader) and the real loader partitions the roster into chunks within the cap, so the join is not a request the loader ever makes. Citing the join 404 as missing modules, or as evidence for any conclusion at all, earns no credit. Naming the cap by constant or by the 3 KB value, and partition/chunk wording, are equivalent.

Keep the simultaneous bugs separate. From console-excerpt.txt, the repeated dsh-paste-input fold-skipped (parse failed) warnings are an unrelated paste-input marker-parsing bug of their own, not the cause of the content-read failure (the end-marker spelling mismatch and the already-shipped fix are welcome detail but not mandatory). From boot-manifest-excerpt.txt, the alpha.2 roster change replacing ui-sidebar-textpreview with ui-sidebar-documentpreview does not explain the empty session-scoped tab either — that tab still opens and claims the address; the rename can at most account for the absolute-scope claim dialog. Conflating the fold warnings with the resource failure, or blaming the sidebar rename for the empty content, earns no credit.

Order the maintainer actions per discussion-excerpt.txt: restart the host once first as the cheap step (the alpha.1 round self-healed a roster/combo mismatch on a later boot), then roll back to the previous published version as the escape hatch (the verified npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.3-alpha.2), keeping the rollback while the forensics go upstream to discussion #5999 — and explicitly refuse plugin-side workarounds: no rewrite, retry, fallback or repair of the unavailable service, because the gap is host-side and the plugin code is not at fault. Package the upstream report with the named forensics — the per-module sweep (62/62 200 means static serving is complete), the contrast reader, the roster excerpt and the invalid-join caveat — and propose a boot-time fail-loud check such as roster-versus-served-combo consistency or a named error when a rostered module is absent from the served bytes, instead of a silent empty tab. A plugin-side fix as the chosen remedy, a restart-only plan without the rollback hatch, or a generic add-logging prevention earns no credit. Rollback/revert/previous-version wording is equivalent.

README.md.text:
# Evidence pack — exam material only, do not modify

Read-only evidence from a real 2026-09-09 dsh 0.1.5-alpha.1 → 0.1.5-alpha.2 in-place
upgrade on Windows (npm global; profile created under 0.1.2/0.1.3 with six external
client plugins junction-linked). The report goes to /app/agent-output/<task-id>/.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| symptom-log.txt | the timeline: two distinct dialogs (absolute-scope claim error on alpha.1; session-scoped 内容读取失败 on alpha.2), the terminal output, the F12 observation |
| boot-manifest-excerpt.txt | the __DSH_BOOT__ roster excerpt: which sidebar/workspace-files modules the 0.1.5-alpha.2 host lists, and the ui-sidebar-textpreview absence (renamed in alpha.2) |
| combo-probe.txt | the per-module sweep (62/62 HTTP 200) plus the all-entries-joined probe (404) |
| contrast-probe.txt | two readers of the same file: file-trace's own RPC (works) vs the sidebar tab's read (never arrives) |
| console-excerpt.txt | the browser console: no documentpreview errors; only dsh-paste-input fold-skip warnings |
| discussion-excerpt.txt | the 0.1.5-alpha.1 round of the same failure family (discussion #5999) |

Host-side notes (0.1.5-alpha.2 tree):
- The workspace-files host row IS in the web-app bundle patch
  (cordis.patch.yml: "- id: workspace-files / name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files'").
- The service resolves each session's workspace root via a typert lookups.register entry
  (sessions.get(sessionId)?.header.cwd, falling back to sandboxPolicy.workspaceRoot).
- Files OUTSIDE the session workspace are allowed ("files outside it are allowed" —
  index.ts read() doc), so .dsh/tmp being under the workspace root is not the blocker.

discussion-excerpt.txt.text:
# Prior art — the same failure family on 0.1.5-alpha.1 (2026-09-09)

deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness discussion #5999
(https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5999)
documents the 0.1.5-alpha.1 round of the same failure family on this deployment:

- An npm-global in-place upgrade onto a profile created under 0.1.2/0.1.3 left the
  client roster and the served combo inconsistent: the boot roster listed the
  newly-added ui-sidebar-* modules but the combo route answered 404 for them at the
  same rev (old modules 200 at that rev) — so every client plugin failed with
  "loaded without registering" (the first unregistered entry, client-hmr, named
  innocently).
- A host restart self-healed the roster/combo mismatch once (the newly-added rows
  entered the roster), but the sidebar tab's content read STILL failed on that boot
  (文件资源服务不可用) — the resource-provider chain did not take over.
- Rollback to the previous published version (npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.3-alpha.2)
  was verified as the escape hatch.

The 0.1.5-alpha.2 round on the same profile shows a related-but-narrower symptom:
modules serve individually (62/62 probes 200), the documentpreview tab opens, but the
file resource metadata still never arrives. The forensics were appended to #5999 as
round 2 (comment 18371079).

symptom-log.txt.text:
# Symptom log — dsh 0.1.5-alpha.2, Windows 11, npm-global in-place upgrade
# (profile created under 0.1.2/0.1.3; six external client plugins junction-linked)

## Timeline

1. npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-alpha.2, then dsh web restart.
   Boot output: "[dsh-profiles] ready", web URL printed. No visible errors in the terminal.

2. Clicking a chat file link whose address is OUTSIDE the session workspace:

   sidebarRight: no registered tab type claims
   "dsh-resource://file/absolute/E:/deepseek-harness/dsh-input-history/package.json"

   (dialog: 无法打开文件 / 重试)

3. The assistant then writes a test file INSIDE the session workspace:

   E:\deepseek-harness\test-lhh010\.dsh\tmp\sidebar-open-test-2.md

   Clicking THAT link opens a right-Sidebar tab titled "sidebar-open-test-2.md" —
   progress over the earlier dialog. But the tab's content area shows only:

   文件资源服务不可用。

   No error message, no retry hint. The file-trace plugin's own RPC reads the same
   file fine in its panel (原文/阅读 modes both show the content).

4. F12 Console: no red errors from documentpreview or the sidebar; the only warnings
   are from dsh-paste-input ("fold skipped (parse failed)" — see console-excerpt.txt).

5. Per-module probe of all 62 manifest entries (see combo-probe.txt): every one returns
   HTTP 200. Zero 404s.
